subject: BlueCrest SOC 2 -- hosting eligibility & bridge-letter options
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@bluecresthealth.com>

Cc: BlueCrest Procurement <procurement@bluecresthealth.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: SOC 2 Type II coverage for hosting options

Hi Marissa,

We are finalizing the security review for an upcoming procurement and need clarification on what Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report covers for different hosting modes. Specifically:

- Does the report cover the Hosted API (api.redwood.com) and the standard model endpoints?
- Are Redwood Dedicated pools (reserved GPU pools) included in the report scope, or do they require separate coverage/bridge letters?
- For Private deployments (VPC/on‑prem packages), what evidence or bridge letters can Redwood provide if the environment is customer‑managed?

Also please confirm the audit period for the most recent Type II, what sample endpoints are included, and whether you can provide a template bridge letter or an attestation we can send to our auditors. We are targeting a procurement decision by the end of May and would appreciate a short answer plus any artifacts you can share.

Thanks,
Alice Turner
Senior IT Compliance Manager
BlueCrest Health
alice.turner@bluecresthealth.com
+1 415 555 0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@bluecresthealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SOC 2 Type II coverage for hosting options

Hi Alice — thanks for reaching out and for the timeline. Short answers up front, then a couple of clarifying questions:

1) Hosted API: INCLUDED in our SOC 2 Type II (audit period listed below).
2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): SOMETIMES included — it depends on whether the Dedicated pool is provisioned and managed by Redwood as part of our managed offering (tenant isolation and dedicated allocation) or if the customer is running hardware that we do not control. If Redwood manages the nodes and network, we can include the pool in scope; we need pool IDs and tenant tags to map to the audit.
3) Private / VPC / on‑prem: Typically OUT OF SCOPE for Redwood's Type II when the infrastructure, networking, or key management is customer‑managed. However, we provide SOC2‑based bridge letters and a controls mapping for private deployments that auditors accept in many cases.

Audit period for our latest Type II: 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31 (we can share the report PDF).

What we need from you to proceed:
- Which hosting mode(s) will your workload use? (Hosted API, Named Dedicated Pool IDs, or Private VPC / on‑prem).
- For Dedicated pools: list the pool IDs or account tags you plan to use.
- For Private/VPC: indicate whether Redwood will manage the control plane or if BlueCrest will run the control plane and networking. Also let us know if you require KMS/HSM proofs for key custody.

I'll loop in Karthik (security) and Laura (legal) to provide detailed artifact lists and a bridge‑letter template. I attached a high‑level sample of the report we can share plus a template for a bridge letter; if you prefer a redlined attestation for your auditors we can also produce that.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Health
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@bluecresthealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SOC 2 Type II coverage for hosting options

Alice — quick technical note from security to make the scope mechanics clear: 

- Hosted API (api.redwood.com) is in‑scope. The auditors sampled production endpoints and control owners for that environment. Sample endpoints are included in the report appendix (we'll share the PDF).

- Dedicated pools: if the pool is a Redwood‑managed resource (we provision and maintain the VMs/GPU instances and network for you) then it is possible to include those pools in our SOC 2 scope. To include a Dedicated pool in the next audit cycle we need: pool identifiers, the start date when the pool went live, and confirmation that no customer‑managed physical access or unmanaged third‑party network links exist. For already‑audited periods, auditors require evidence that the pool was live and managed during the audit window to be considered sampled.

- Private/VPC/on‑prem: these are usually customer‑managed boundaries. In those cases we produce a controls mapping and a bridge letter describing which Redwood controls can be considered applicable and which controls are the customer's responsibility. We do not extend our Type II opinion to environments where we do not control the infrastructure and logical access.

Artifacts we can provide immediately: SOC2‑TypeII‑Redwood‑2026.pdf (redacted to remove customer names), a Bridge‑Letter template, and an Endpoint Sample Guide describing the kinds of endpoints auditors expect to see.

If BlueCrest confirms specific Dedicated pool IDs we will correlate the pools to the audit evidence (change logs, patching records, access lists). For private deployments we can prepare a signed bridge letter with the exact control mapping within 3‑5 business days once we have the environment details.

— Karthik
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
